mainTopic: The drill-hole versus סלע measure for a skull, the testimony of חזקיה אבי עקש about vessels with no inside, and the משנה on eye blemishes
overview: The amud opens at the end of a challenge: the drill-hole measure of בית שמאי seems to equal the סלע of בית הלל, so the two would not really disagree. רב חסדא answers that the measure is a hole with room for the drill itself, and רב תחליפא says this is as certain as the testimony of חזקיה אבי עקש. The גמרא then quotes that testimony about vessels with no inside, and רבי יצחק בר אבין re-reads it as being about a כלי שטף rather than a כלי חרס. This leads to a long back-and-forth. Impure liquids make a vessel טמא only by rabbinic law, and the רבנן modeled this rule on a כלי חרס as a sign, so people would not burn תרומה and קדשים. The case is limited to vessels used for sitting, which can get מדרס, something a כלי חרס never gets. The גמרא then returns to the skull: רב פפא and later רב נחמן explain the sizes so that בית שמאי are truly the strict side, using the larger סלע of Nero. Finally, a new משנה lists blemishes of the eye and eyelid and defines a תבלול.

steps.title: The measure equals the hole of a yoke
steps.stepSummary: The challenge ends: the measure being discussed comes out the same as the hole of a yoke, the size of a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the full size of the hole of a yoke!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge from the lines before this. It shows that the measure of a מקדח comes out equal to a סלע, the size of the hole in a yoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב תחליפא tied the סלע to the hole of a yoke. If the מקדח of בית שמאי is that same size, there is no real difference between the two measures. This would erase the dispute, so the challenge needs an answer.

phrases.english: Like the full size of the hole of a yoke!

steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the מקדח measure is different from a סלע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both measures come out equal to the hole of a yoke, so the two opinions would not really differ.

steps.title: רב חסדא suggests a drilled hole with its blocking edges cleared
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא is silent, and רב חסדא suggests the measure is a drilled hole widened by clearing away the edges that block the drill.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא was silent. רב חסדא said to him: Perhaps we learned 'a drilled hole and what blocks it,' meaning the hole with its edges cleared.
steps.whatsHappening: רב תחליפא has no answer. רב חסדא offers one: the measure is a drilled hole that has room for the drill itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole that the drill can be put into and taken out of is a little bigger than the bare hole. So the מקדח measure is slightly larger than a סלע, and the two measures are no longer the same.

keyTerms.meaning: a drill, or the hole a drill makes
what blocks it: the edges of the hole that get in the drill's way, cleared so the drill goes in and out freely

phrases.english: He was silent, and Rav Chisda said to him:
phrases.notes: The one who was silent is רב תחליפא.

phrases.english: Perhaps we learned 'a drilled hole and what blocks it.'
phrases.notes: He means a hole big enough for the drill to go in and come out, which is a bit bigger than a סלע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקדח is just the bare drilled hole, the same as a סלע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מקדח includes room for the drill itself, so it is slightly larger.

steps.title: Not perhaps, but certainly
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא confirms that the reading is certainly correct and compares its reliability to the testimony of חזקיה אבי עקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא said to him: Do not say 'perhaps.' Say it is certainly 'a drilled hole and what blocks it.' One can rely on it like חזקיה אבי עקש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב תחליפא agrees with רב חסדא and makes it stronger. This is not a guess; it is certain. He also points to a well-known teaching, which the גמרא will quote next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's suggestion becomes a firm explanation. Comparing it to חזקיה אבי עקש shows it is as reliable as that famous testimony. The mention of the testimony sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: to hang on, to rely on
a תנא whose testimony was well known

steps.whatToRemember: The measure of a מקדח means a hole the drill can enter and leave, a bit more than the bare hole.

phrases.english: And Rav Tachlifa said to him:
Do not say 'perhaps,'
rather, certainly 'a drilled hole and what blocks it,'
one should rely on it
like Chizkiyah the father of Ikkesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms and strengthens רב חסדא's answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מקדח measure is certainly a drilled hole with room for its drill.

steps.title: The testimony of חזקיה אבי עקש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the testimony: a כלי חרס with no inside has no separate rules for its outside, so טומאה on either side makes the whole vessel טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: חזקיה אבי עקש gave this testimony before רבן גמליאל in יבנה, in the name of רבן גמליאל הזקן: Any כלי חרס that has no inside has no separate rule for its back. If its inside became טמא, its back is טמא. If its back became טמא, its inside is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the testimony that רב תחליפא mentioned. It is about a clay vessel that has no hollow inside, such as a flat clay plate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כלי חרס becomes טמא only from its inside, and its outside follows a different rule. Here, a clay vessel with no inside is treated as one whole: טומאה on either side makes all of it טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: the inside, the hollow part that holds things
the back or outside of a vessel

steps.confusionAlert: On a plain reading, the testimony seems to say that a כלי חרס with no inside can become טמא. The next step challenges exactly this, and step 6 re-reads the testimony as being about a כלי שטף, not a כלי חרס.

phrases.english: As we learned: This testimony was given by
Chizkiyah the father of Ikkesh
before Rabban Gamliel in Yavneh,
which he said in the name of Rabban Gamliel the Elder:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס —
phrases.english: Any earthenware vessel that has no inside —
has no back that is treated separately.
If its inside became impure — its back is impure,
if its back became impure — its inside is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: זוֹ עֵדוּת הֵעִיד חִזְקִיָּה אֲבִי עִקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the testimony that step 3 mentioned
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי חרס with no inside becomes טמא as one whole; טומאה on either side makes it all טמא.

steps.title: The Torah ties a clay vessel's impurity to its inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the testimony: the תורה makes a כלי חרס become טמא only through its inside, so a vessel with no inside should not become טמא at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a כלי חרס, the תורה made it depend on its inside. If it has an inside, it becomes טמא. If it has no inside, it does not become טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the testimony it just quoted. A פסוק links the טומאה of a clay vessel to its inside, so how can a vessel with no inside become טמא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of something falling 'into its inside.' This suggests that a clay vessel with no inside is not able to become טמא at all. That clashes with חזקיה's testimony, which says it does become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: the תורה made it depend on

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge forces the גמרא to re-read the testimony. The next step answers it by moving the rule from a כלי חרס to a כלי שטף.

phrases.english: An earthenware vessel: the Merciful One made it depend on its inside —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:33

phrases.english: if it has an inside — it becomes impure,

phrases.aramaic: לֵית לֵיהּ תּוֹךְ — לָא אִיטַּמִּי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: if it has no inside — it does not become impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the testimony quoted in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה אבי עקש's ruling that a כלי חרס with no inside becomes טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק makes a clay vessel's טומאה depend on its inside, so a vessel without an inside should never become טמא.

steps.title: The testimony is really about a rinsed vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבין reads the testimony as being about a כלי שטף that matches a כלי חרס with no inside. Such a vessel has no separate outside, so טומאה on either side makes the whole thing טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבין said: This is what the testimony means. Take a shape that would count as 'no inside' if it were a כלי חרס. The matching vessel made of rinsed material, a כלי שטף, has no separate back. If its inside became טמא, its outside is טמא. If its outside became טמא, its inside is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אבין answers the question from step 5 by saying the testimony is not about a כלי חרס at all. It is about a כלי שטף shaped like a כלי חרס that has no inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי חרס with no inside never becomes טמא, so the challenge in step 5 was correct about it. But a כלי שטף, such as a wooden vessel, can become טמא even without an inside. For that kind of vessel, the testimony teaches that there is no split between inside and outside: טומאה anywhere makes all of it טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (the גמרא is re-reading a statement)
A 'rinsed vessel': one that is purified by immersion in a מקוה, such as wood or metal
The back or outside of a vessel
Its back, meaning its outer surface

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying a כלי חרס with no inside becomes טמא. It never does. The rule about inside and outside sharing טומאה is only about the matching כלי שטף.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avin said:
This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס —
phrases.english: Anything that would have no inside in an earthenware vessel —
phrases.notes: Such a כלי חרס can't become טמא at all, so he moves the rule over to the matching wooden-type vessel.

phrases.english: its counterpart in a rinsed vessel
has no back that is treated separately;
if its inside became impure, its outside became impure;
if its outside became impure, its inside became impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אָבִין: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by re-reading the testimony.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-interpretation: the subject of the testimony is moved from a כלי חרס to a כלי שטף.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The testimony seemed to say that a כלי חרס with no inside becomes טמא, which goes against the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The testimony is about a כלי שטף matching a כלי חרס with no inside. That vessel can become טמא, and its inside and outside are not separated.

steps.title: Why mention the earthenware vessel at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the testimony ties the rule to a כלי חרס, if it could simply have stated the rule about a כלי שטף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need to connect it to a כלי חרס? Just say: any כלי שטף that has no inside has no separate back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of the testimony as רבי יצחק בר אבין explained it. If the rule is about a כלי שטף, mentioning a כלי חרס seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new reading, the כלי חרס adds nothing to the law. So the extra wording looks pointless, and the גמרא expects every word to teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: To make it depend on, or tie it to

phrases.english: Why do I need to tie it to an earthenware vessel?

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי שֶׁטֶף —
phrases.english: Let it say: any rinsed vessel that has no inside —
has no back that is treated separately!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording that results from רבי יצחק בר אבין's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The mention of כלי חרס in the testimony as re-read in step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the law is only about a כלי שטף, the reference to a כלי חרס is extra wording.

steps.title: A rinsed vessel with an inside is like earthenware
steps.stepSummary: Mentioning a כלי חרס teaches that a כלי שטף that does have an inside follows the כלי חרס rule. Its outside becomes טמא only if its inside becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that if it has an inside, it is like a כלי חרס. A כלי חרס works this way: if its inside became טמא, its outside is טמא, and if its inside did not become טמא, its outside is not טמא. So too a כלי שטף: if its inside became טמא, its outside is טמא, and if its inside did not become טמא, its outside is not טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the comparison to a כלי חרס teaches a second rule. When a כלי שטף has an inside, its טומאה works like a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison works in both directions. With no inside, the כלי שטף has no split between its sides, as in step 6. With an inside, it follows a כלי חרס: the inside decides everything. If the inside is טמא the whole vessel is טמא, and if only the outside touched טומאה, the vessel is not fully טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Just as... so too... (a comparison pattern)
It is like, it has the same status as

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, a כלי שטף with no inside has no split between its sides. A כלי שטף with an inside acts like a כלי חרס: its outside follows its inside.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ תּוֹךְ — הֲרֵי הוּא כִּכְלִי חֶרֶס;
phrases.english: that if it has an inside, it is like an earthenware vessel.
phrases.notes: 'It' here is the rinsed vessel, the כלי שטף.

phrases.english: Just as with an earthenware vessel,
if its inside became impure, its outside became impure,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — לֹא נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ;
phrases.english: and if its inside did not become impure, its outside did not become impure;
so too with a rinsed vessel:
if its inside became impure, its outside became impure,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — לֹא נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ.
phrases.english: and if its inside did not become impure, its outside did not become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by finding a teaching in the mention of כלי חרס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra wording teaches a new rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning a כלי חרס seemed to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that a כלי שטף with an inside follows the כלי חרס pattern: its outside follows its inside.

steps.title: The תורה said 'its inside' only about earthenware
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 8. The תורה made טומאה depend on the inside only for a כלי חרס, so why should a כלי שטף follow that rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a כלי חרס, because the תורה revealed 'its inside' about it. But for a כלי שטף, did the תורה reveal 'its inside'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the comparison it just made. The rule that the inside is what counts comes from a פסוק written only about a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a כלי חרס, the תורה clearly says טומאה works through its inside. For a כלי שטף there is no such פסוק. So it seems that touching any part of it, outside included, should make it טמא, and step 8's comparison has no source.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for... (opening of a challenge that contrasts two cases)

phrases.english: It makes sense for an earthenware vessel,
since the Merciful One revealed 'its inside' about it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:33

phrases.english: but for a rinsed vessel,
did the Merciful One reveal 'its inside' about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא כְּלִי חֶרֶס, גַּלִּי בֵּיהּ רַחֲמָנָא תּוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that a כלי שטף with an inside follows the כלי חרס rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'inside' rule comes from a פסוק written only about a כלי חרס. Without a matching פסוק, a כלי שטף should become טמא through any contact, outside included.

steps.title: The case is rabbinic impurity from liquids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that for תורה-level טומאה a כלי שטף does not follow the כלי חרס rule. It says the case is טומאה from liquids, which is only רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we were talking about טומאה from the תורה, you would be right. But here we are talking about טומאה from liquids, which is only from the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9 by saying the testimony is about rabbinic טומאה, not תורה טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 asked why a כלי שטף should copy a rule that the תורה gave only to a כלי חרס. The answer accepts that at the תורה level it would not. The case is impure liquids touching the vessel, and that טומאה comes only from the רבנן, so the רבנן can set its rules.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not taking back the idea from step 8. It is only limiting it to טומאה from liquids, which comes from the רבנן.

phrases.english: If it is about Torah-level impurity, indeed so,
phrases.notes: He means: you are right that at the תורה level, a כלי שטף would not follow the כלי חרס rule.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
With the impurity of liquids, which is rabbinic,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּטוּמְאָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא — הָכִי נָמֵי, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by limiting the case to rabbinic טומאה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (הכא במאי עסקינן) to rabbinic טומאה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was about תורה-level טומאה, where a כלי שטף should not follow the כלי חרס rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is טומאה from liquids, which is rabbinic, so the רבנן could apply the כלי חרס pattern.

steps.title: A משנה shows liquid impurity can stay on the outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: if impure liquid touches only the outside of a vessel, only the outside is טמא. If the inside is touched, the whole vessel is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: a vessel whose outside became טמא from liquids has only its outside טמא. Its inside, rim, ear-handle and handles stay טהור. If its inside became טמא, the whole vessel is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show that this rule of 'outside only' really exists for liquid טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of any vessel, not only a כלי חרס. It shows that for liquid טומאה, an impure outside does not spread to the inside, but an impure inside spreads everywhere. This is the כלי חרס pattern that step 8 described.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
A vessel whose outside became impure through liquids,
its outside is impure,
its inside, its rim, its ear-handle, and its handles are pure.
If its inside became impure, the whole thing is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 10 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That liquid טומאה follows the 'outside only unless the inside' pattern.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כלים about a vessel whose outside became טמא through liquids.

steps.title: Liquids make vessels impure only by rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: By תורה law, food and liquids do not make a vessel טמא. The רבנן decreed it because of the liquids of a זב and זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: By תורה law, food does not make a vessel טמא, and liquid does not make a vessel טמא. The רבנן decreed it because of the liquids of a זב and a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why liquid טומאה on a vessel is only rabbinic. This sets up the reason for the special rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the תורה level, an impure liquid cannot make a vessel טמא at all. The רבנן added this rule because people might confuse it with the liquids of a זב or זבה, like spit or urine, which do make vessels טמא by תורה law. Since it is a rabbinic rule, the רבנן can give it its own shape.

keyTerms.meaning: food does not make a vessel impure
the bodily liquids of a man or woman with a זיבה discharge, which are a source of טומאה

phrases.english: By Torah law, food does not make a vessel impure,
and a liquid does not make a vessel impure,
and it is the Sages who decreed it
because of the liquid of a זב and a זבה.
phrases.notes: Their liquids, like spit or urine, really do make vessels טמא by תורה law, so the רבנן worried people would mix them up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the liquid טומאה in step 10 and step 11 is only rabbinic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food and liquids do not make vessels טמא by תורה law. It is a rabbinic decree because of the liquids of a זב and זבה.

steps.title: The Sages modeled it on a כלי חרס
steps.stepSummary: Because this טומאה is rabbinic, the רבנן treated a כלי שטף like a כלי חרס, not like its own תורה-level rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the רבנן treated it like the טומאה of a כלי חרס, and not like the תורה-level טומאה of the vessel itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the result: for this rabbinic טומאה, the רבנן chose to copy the כלי חרס rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By its own תורה rule, a כלי שטף that is טמא on the outside becomes טמא all over. For rabbinic liquid טומאה, the רבנן instead used the כלי חרס rule, so an impure outside does not make the inside טמא. This fully answers the question of step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: they made it like, they treated it as

steps.whatToRemember: Liquid טומאה on a vessel is only rabbinic. For it, the רבנן made even a כלי שטף follow the כלי חרס rule: outside only, unless the inside becomes טמא.

phrases.english: Therefore, the Sages made it
like the impurity of an earthenware vessel,
and the Sages did not make it
like its own Torah-level impurity.
phrases.notes: He means the כלי שטף's own תורה rule, where טומאה on the outside makes the whole vessel טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ, שַׁוְּיוּהּ רַבָּנַן כְּטוּמְאָה דִּכְלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result from step 12 and finishes the answer to step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כלי שטף can only follow its own תורה rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: For rabbinic liquid טומאה, the רבנן chose the כלי חרס pattern.

steps.title: A sign so people won't burn תרומה and קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן made a sign to show the טומאה is only rabbinic, so people would not burn תרומה and קדשים that touched such a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן made a sign so that people would not burn תרומה and קדשים because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason the רבנן chose the כלי חרס rule here: to mark this טומאה as only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rabbinic rule looked exactly like the תורה rule, people might treat things that touched the vessel as truly טמא and burn them. Burning תרומה or קדשים that are טהור by תורה law is forbidden. Leaving the inside טהור shows everyone that this is a lighter, rabbinic טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: a sign, a marker to tell things apart
the holy portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: the רבנן sometimes shape their rules a little differently from תורה rules on purpose, so people can tell the two apart.

phrases.english: The Sages made a sign,
so that one will not burn
because of it תרומה and holy offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the rabbinic choice in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was no reason for the רבנן to change the vessel's usual rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The change is a sign that protects תרומה and קדשים from being burned for no reason.

steps.title: Then why no sign for a vessel with no inside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the רבנן made a sign, they should also make one for a vessel with no inside. Yet the testimony says it becomes טמא all over.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a vessel with no inside should also get a sign!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation by pointing back to the testimony about a vessel with no inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said a כלי שטף like a כלי חרס with no inside becomes טמא all over from either side. If this is rabbinic liquid טומאה and the רבנן wanted a sign, they should have made one there too, for example by leaving some part טהור. So why did the testimony say it is all טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: it has no inside, it cannot hold anything

phrases.english: If so,
a vessel that has no inside, too,
let them also make a sign for it!
phrases.notes: This points back to the testimony in step 6, which said such a vessel becomes טמא all over.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ נָמֵי, לֶיעְבֵּיד נָמֵי הֶיכֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the היכירא reason of step 14 using the case from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן made a sign for rabbinic liquid טומאה (step 14), together with the testimony as read in step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the sign is needed for rabbinic liquid טומאה, it should also apply to a vessel with no inside. But the testimony says that vessel becomes טמא all over.

steps.title: One sign is enough to show the whole decree is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: Since the רבנן made a sign for vessels that have an inside, everyone will know that a vessel with no inside is also only rabbinically טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the רבנן made a sign for a vessel that has an inside, it is known that a vessel with no inside is also only טמא מדרבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15: why didn't the רבנן make a sign for a vessel with no inside too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign is that only the outside becomes טמא when only the outside was touched. That sign already shows people that this whole decree is only rabbinic. So there is no need for a second sign, and people will understand that the vessel with no inside is rabbinic too, and they will not burn תרומה or קדשים because of it.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel that has an inside, so it can hold things
A vessel with no inside, like a flat board

phrases.english: Since they made a sign
for a vessel that has an inside,
phrases.notes: The sign is the rule from steps 13 and 14: if only the outside is touched, only the outside becomes טמא.

phrases.english: it is known that a vessel with no inside is rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּעֲבַדוּ הֶיכֵּירָא בְּיֵשׁ לוֹ תּוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: One sign covers the whole category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each kind of vessel would need its own sign
steps.terutzMaskana: The sign on vessels with an inside already shows that the entire decree is rabbinic

steps.title: Can a vessel with no inside become טמא at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a rinsable vessel with no inside cannot become טמא even by תורה law, because a vessel must be like a sack, which is carried both full and empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rinsable vessel with no inside: can it become טמא by תורה law? We need it to be like a sack. Just as a sack is carried full and empty, so too anything must be carried full and empty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole case: a vessel with no inside does not seem able to become טמא at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists a sack among things that can become טמא. From this we learn that a vessel must be something carried both full and empty. A vessel with no inside can never be 'full,' so it seems it cannot become טמא by תורה law at all. So why would the רבנן's decree make it טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel made pure by rinsing (wood, metal, leather), unlike earthenware
Carried around both full and empty

phrases.english: And a rinsable vessel with no inside,
can it receive טומאה by Torah law?
We need it to be like a sack,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:32

phrases.english: just as a sack is carried full and empty,
so too anything that is carried full and empty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי שֶׁטֶף, דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא בַּר קַבּוֹלֵי טוּמְאָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case discussed in steps 15-16
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a כלי שטף with no inside becomes טמא from liquids
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vessel must be like a sack, carried full and empty; a vessel with no inside cannot be carried full, so it should not be able to become טמא at all

steps.title: It means vessels used for sitting or lying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is vessels fit for מדרס, which can become טמא even without an inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about those vessels that are fit for מדרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case to vessels used for sitting or lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'sack' rule applies to ordinary vessels. But things made for sitting or lying can become טמא through מדרס even without an inside. Since these vessels can become טמא by תורה law, the רבנן's decree about liquids can apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: טומאה passed on when a זב, זבה, or נדה sits, lies, or leans on an item

phrases.english: It refers to those vessels that are fit for מדרס.
phrases.notes: He means things a person would sit or lie on, like a stool or a board for lying on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was any vessel with no inside, which cannot become טמא by Torah law
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is vessels fit for מדרס, which can become טמא even with no inside

steps.title: Then earthenware should be included too
steps.stepSummary: If the decree covers vessels with no inside that are fit for sitting, then earthenware vessels with no inside that are fit for sitting should also be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, earthenware too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said the decree is about no-inside vessels used for sitting. The same could be true of an earthenware piece with no inside that someone sits on. So why should the decree not apply to earthenware too?

phrases.english: If so, earthenware too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the decree covers vessels fit for מדרס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Earthenware with no inside could also be sat on, so the decree should apply to it as well

steps.title: Earthenware never becomes טמא through מדרס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that earthenware vessels cannot get מדרס טומאה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no מדרס for earthenware vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earthenware challenge and closes this back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earthenware becomes טמא only through its inside space. It never becomes טמא through מדרס. So a flat earthenware piece used for sitting cannot become טמא by תורה law, and the רבנן had no reason to include it in their decree.

keyTerms.meaning: An earthenware vessel, which becomes טמא only from its inside
The rule that earthenware never gets מדרס טומאה
A man with a certain bodily flow whose sitting or lying causes מדרס

steps.whatToRemember: The decree about liquids making vessels טמא is rabbinic. For a כלי שטף with no inside, it applies only to things used for sitting or lying, which can get מדרס. It does not apply to earthenware, which never gets מדרס.

phrases.english: There is no מדרס for earthenware vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the two cases are different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Earthenware fit for sitting is the same as a כלי שטף fit for sitting
steps.terutzMaskana: Earthenware cannot get מדרס at all, so it is not included

steps.title: רב פפא: the סלע measure refers to a large drill
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the earlier question about a skull, רב פפא says the teaching that a drill hole equals a סלע was about a large drill.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We learned this about a large drill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier question about how big a piece missing from a skull must be, and רב פפא gives a new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a teaching that a drill hole is the size of a סלע, which made it seem that בית שמאי (drill hole) and בית הלל (סלע) do not disagree. רב פפא says that teaching was about a large drill. A regular drill hole is smaller than a סלע, so the two opinions really do disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives an answer here
We learned (in a ברייתא or משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not about vessels at all. The גמרא has jumped back to the earlier question about a skull missing a piece.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
We learned this about a large drill.
phrases.notes: He means the teaching that a drill hole equals a סלע was talking about a big drill, not a regular one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מַקְדֵּחַ גָּדוֹל שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about vessels and returns to the earlier question about the skull
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the size in the teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any drill hole equals a סלע, so בית שמאי and בית הלל do not disagree
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a large drill equals a סלע; a regular drill hole is smaller, so there is a real disagreement

steps.title: So an ordinary drill hole is smaller than a סלע
steps.stepSummary: From רב פפא's answer, the גמרא concludes that an ordinary, unspecified drill hole is smaller than a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: This shows that an ordinary drill is also smaller than a סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from what רב פפא just said: if only a LARGE drill equals a סלע, then a regular drill must be smaller. This conclusion sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said that the teaching 'a drill hole equals a סלע' was about a large drill. So the plain 'drill' that בית שמאי mention in the skull case is smaller than the סלע that בית הלל mention. The next steps test whether this fits each opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: A drill, or the size of the hole a drill makes
A coin, used here as a measure of size

phrases.english: By implication, an ordinary drill hole
is also smaller than a סלע.
phrases.notes: He means the plain drill בית שמאי mention in the skull case. It is smaller than the סלע בית הלל mention.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּמַקְדֵּחַ סְתָם זוּטַרא נָמֵי מִכְּסֶלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the logical result of רב פפא's answer that only a large drill equals a סלע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified drill hole is smaller than a סלע.

steps.title: This works for רבי מאיר but not for the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion fits רבי מאיר, who says בית שמאי meant a small doctors' drill. But the חכמים say they meant the large chamber drill, which equals a סלע. Then there is no difference between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is fine for רבי מאיר, but what can you say for the חכמים? As we learned: Which drill did they mean? The small drill of doctors, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: the large drill of the chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion. It quotes a משנה showing that the חכמים think בית שמאי meant a large drill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, בית שמאי meant a small doctors' drill, which really is smaller than a סלע, so the two sides differ. For the חכמים, בית שמאי meant the large chamber drill. רב פפא said a large drill equals a סלע, so בית שמאי and בית הלל would be giving the same size, and there would be nothing to argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (a challenge)
Doctors; their drill is small, used on bones
The chamber in the Temple, where a large drill was kept

phrases.english: This works out well according to רבי מאיר,
but according to the Rabbis, what is there to say?
As we learned: which drill did they mean?
phrases.notes: אהלות 2:3. 'They' are בית שמאי, talking about the skull.

phrases.english: The small drill of doctors,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the Sages say: the large one of the chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the inference of step 22 against the two opinions about which drill בית שמאי meant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an ordinary drill is smaller than a סלע, together with רב פפא's statement that a large drill equals a סלע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the חכמים, בית שמאי meant a large drill, which equals a סלע. Then both sides give the same size, and there is no argument at all.

steps.title: Even for רבי מאיר there is a problem
steps.stepSummary: If בית שמאי's drill is smaller than a סלע, then בית שמאי are the lenient side here. That case is not on the fixed list of places where בית שמאי are lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even for רבי מאיר, does it really work? It would become one of the leniencies of בית שמאי and stringencies of בית הלל. And we have a rule: what we learned, we learned, and what we did not learn, we did not learn!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back the 'it works for רבי מאיר' and shows a problem with his opinion too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Think about a skull missing a piece that is bigger than a small drill but smaller than a סלע. בית שמאי would say it is no longer טמא, which is lenient, while בית הלל still say it is טמא. But there is a set list (in עדיות) of cases where בית שמאי are lenient, and only those count. Since this case is not on the list, בית שמאי cannot be the lenient side here.

keyTerms.term: קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
keyTerms.meaning: The special list of cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict

keyTerms.term: דִּתְנַן תְּנַן, דְּלָא תְּנַן לָא תְּנַן
keyTerms.meaning: Only the cases listed count; nothing can be added to the list

steps.confusionAlert: Usually בית שמאי are the strict side. The list of 'leniencies of בית שמאי' is a short, closed list of exceptions, so any explanation that makes them lenient somewhere else causes a problem.

phrases.english: And according to רבי מאיר, does it work out well?
It would be one of the leniencies of בית שמאי
and the stringencies of בית הלל.
phrases.notes: This is the list in משנה עדיות of places where בית שמאי are the lenient side.

phrases.english: And we: what we learned, we learned,
and what we did not learn, we did not learn!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the challenge: the problem is not only for the חכמים but also for רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's view that בית שמאי meant a small drill, smaller than a סלע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the drill is smaller than a סלע, בית שמאי become the lenient side in the skull case. That would add a case to the closed list of בית שמאי's leniencies, which is not allowed.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The large drill equals the bigger סלע of Nero
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the סלע that equals a large drill is the Nero סלע. An ordinary סלע is smaller than even an ordinary drill, so בית שמאי are the strict side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We learned about a Nero סלע, that it is like a large drill. An ordinary סלע is smaller than an ordinary drill.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers both challenges by saying there are two kinds of סלע: a bigger Nero סלע and a smaller ordinary one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching 'a large drill equals a סלע' was about the bigger Nero סלע. The סלע that בית הלל use is the ordinary one, which is smaller than even an ordinary drill hole. So בית שמאי need a bigger hole before the skull stops being טמא. That makes them the strict side, for both רבי מאיר and the חכמים, and there is a real argument between them.

keyTerms.meaning: A סלע coin from the time of Nero, larger than an ordinary סלע

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sizes of סלע. The Nero סלע equals a large drill, but an ordinary סלע is smaller than any drill. That is why בית שמאי, who measure by a drill, are the strict side in the skull case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the rule that בית שמאי are lenient only in the listed cases. It also gives the two sides a real difference in size according to every opinion.

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
We learned about a Nero סלע,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה about a window, which said a drill hole equals a סלע.

phrases.english: that it is like a large drill hole;
but an ordinary סלע is smaller than an ordinary drill hole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: סֶלַע נִירוֹנִית שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 23 and 24 by redefining which סלע equals a large drill.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the measurement: two different sizes of סלע.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the סלע that equals a large drill is the same ordinary סלע that בית הלל use. That would make an ordinary drill smaller than a סלע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The large drill equals a Nero סלע. An ordinary סלע is smaller than any drill, so בית שמאי are stringent and the two sides really argue.

steps.title: The משנה lists eye and eyelid blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists blemishes of the eyelid and the eye: a pierced, damaged, or split eyelid, and a דק, תבלול, חלזון, נחש, or עצב in the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: An eyelid that was pierced, damaged, or split is a blemish. So is an eye that has a cataract, a תבלול, or a growth shaped like a snail, a snake, or a berry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists more blemishes, this time of the eye and the eyelid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list has two groups. The first is damage to the eyelid: pierced, chipped, or split. The second is growths or marks inside the eye itself. Each one counts as a מום, so a בכור with it may be slaughtered outside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
A thin film over the eye, like a cataract
A white streak in the eye, defined in the next lines
A physical blemish that disqualifies an animal from the altar

steps.whyThisMatters: A בכור may only be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש once it has a real מום, so knowing exactly which marks count has practical weight.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The eyelid that was pierced,
phrases.notes: These are more blemishes that let a בכור be slaughtered outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: that was damaged, that was split;
or if there was in its eye a cataract,
a tevallul, a snail,
phrases.notes: Snail, snake and berry are growths in those shapes that cover part of the eye.

phrases.english: a snake, or a berry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of skull holes and the drill compared to a סלע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damage to the eyelid (pierced, chipped, split) and growths in the eye (דק, תבלול, חלזון, נחש, עצב) are blemishes.

steps.title: The משנה asks what a תבלול is
steps.stepSummary: The משנה stops to ask what exactly a תבלול is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a תבלול?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks for a definition of one term from its list. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most items on the list are easy to picture, but תבלול is not. The משנה asks so it can draw a clear line between a mark that is a מום and one that is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is it? What is it?

phrases.english: What is a tevallul?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of one item from the list in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What physical mark counts as a תבלול.

steps.title: A white streak into the black is a תבלול; black into white is not a blemish
steps.stepSummary: A תבלול is a white streak that crosses the iris and enters the black. A black streak that enters the white is not a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a white streak that cuts across the ring of the eye and goes into the black part. If a black streak goes into the white part, it is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question by defining a תבלול. It then gives a look-alike case that does not count as a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Direction decides the law. White pushing into the black (the pupil) is a תבלול and a מום. Black spreading into the white of the eye is not a מום at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The ring around the pupil, the iris
The black part of the eye
White; here a white streak, or the white of the eye

steps.whatToRemember: תבלול = white going into black, which is a מום. Black going into white is not a מום.
steps.confusionAlert: The two cases sound almost the same. Watch the direction: only white entering the black is a blemish.

phrases.english: A white thread that cuts across the iris
and enters the black.
phrases.notes: The black is the pupil, the center of the eye.

phrases.english: If black enters the white,
it is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A תבלול is a white streak crossing the iris into the black. The reverse, black into white, is not a מום.
